rv.q: Slick and streamlined, the production’s offbeat charm is leavened out by serious themes and sudden twists, making this an enjoyable and engaging experience.
The production ripples with physical activity and streetwise authenticity across the boards.

Pigeon English, Stephen Kelman’s 2011. Man Booker Prize shortlisted novel, is interpreted masterfully for the stage with rawness, humour and a fantastic relatable quality that keeps us as an audience hooked from the explosive curtain up, to final, harrowing scene.
Gbolahan Obisesan ‘s adaptation struggles somewhat with the many narrative strands of the original. It’s long, and it doesn’t focus.
Anna Niland’s production has a climbing frame set, designed by Cecilia Carey, and fields exuberant performances from the large NYT cast.

cn.t: Critics praise the National Youth Theatre's energetic production of "Pigeon English," with the young ensemble shining through confident performances and snappy naturalistic dialogue that brings this contemporary story of gang culture to vivid life.
